newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Rising bank shares boost Nigerian stock trade.
newsitem.headline: Rising bank shares boost Nigerian stock trade.

text.p: Shares of leading banks ended higher at the Nigerian stock exchange on Tuesday as investors moved in to reap from new measures to strengthen the financial sector, dealers said.
The all-share index closed at 7772.49 from Monday's 7729.29, helped by impressive performance of the banks and undiminished interest in the market's blue chips.

"Government's order on banks to raise their capital base nine-fold has caused investors to flood the market for bank shares with a view to increasing their holding through bonus and rights issues," one trader said.
Analysts said improved performances by leading banks and the perception that the distress in the sector had ended was also responsible for the rally.
First Bank, closing at 14.50 naira, and Union Bank at 12.50 naira, were 20 kobo higher on Tuesday while Afribank closed 10 kobo up at 6.00 naira.
It was a fine day also for brewery shares as Guinness and Nigerian Breweries recovered some lost grounds. Guinness was 6.85 naira, up 10 kobo and Nigerian Breweries rose 18 kobo to 15.40 naira.
Conglomerates were relatively calm as all but Lever Brothers ended unchanged. It gained 20 kobo, ending at 20.70 naira because brokers said they had orders to buy for large investors.
Oil marketers and food/beverage stocks continued to soar on demand as did insurance and industrial/domestic firms.

In a bid to enjoy capital appreciation, dealers said some investors were buying cheaper shares such as Aluminium Manufacturing company (Alumaco), up 10 kobo at 3.10 naira, Royal Exchange Assurance and Lasaco Assurance which were five kobo higher at 3.50 naira and 1.45 naira, respectively.
